root_cause: The CI image was bumped from python:3.12 to python:3.13, and Python 3.13 removed the deprecated imghdr module (PEP 594). src/uploads.py imports imghdr, so the test module fails to import.
evidence: failure.log: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'imghdr' at src/uploads.py line 1
repo/CHANGELOG.md: 'CI image bumped from python:3.12 to python:3.13.'
imghdr was deprecated in 3.11 and removed in 3.13 (PEP 594)
Local check (Python 3.13): with an 8-byte PNG signature check, test_png passes
patch:
--- a/src/uploads.py
+++ b/src/uploads.py
@@ -1,3 +1,4 @@
-import imghdr
+# imghdr was removed from the standard library in Python 3.13 (PEP 594).
+PNG_SIGNATURE = b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
 def is_png(data: bytes) -> bool:
-    return imghdr.what(None, h=data) == "png"
+    return data[:8] == PNG_SIGNATURE
message_to_human: The python:3.13 image bump broke uploads.py: imghdr was removed from the standard library in 3.13 (PEP 594). This MR replaces imghdr.what(...) == 'png' with a direct check of the 8-byte PNG signature (\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n), the same test imghdr ran for PNG. It has no new dependency and works on 3.12 and 3.13. test_png passes locally on 3.13. If more image formats will be needed later, consider python-magic or Pillow instead. I didn't roll the image back to 3.12, because the upgrade looks intentional.
